palette.notes: Near-black backgrounds with deep blues, violets and teal; small warm accents (red, yellow, pink) for the blob, lamps and items. Clip 1 is unrelated (dog video), clip 2 is a creator talking, only short game shots.

lighting: Darkness is the default; light comes from small sources (lamps, candles, glowing waterfalls) that reveal nearby tiles. Low resolution was a deliberate limit that shapes this lighting.
silhouette: The player is a tiny yellow blob, only a few pixels, readable because it is the warmest thing on a dark cool screen.

motion.timing: Not measured (no metrics file). Frames show slow ambient motion (drifting motes, swinging chains, a yoyo/rope arc) while rooms stay static; much animation is procedural in code.

texture: Blue line-like tile edges on black, CRT/scanline sheen, sparse fireflies and specks, overgrown crumbling architecture.
camera: Fixed single-screen rooms (flip-screen); no scrolling within a room.
sound: Ambient soundtrack and noises carry the eerie mood (per reviews); little music.

acting.enters: The blob emerges from a flower at the start; in rooms it appears from the edge of a fixed screen.
acting.acts: Small hero, huge animals: many creatures are much bigger than the player and some ignore it, so scale itself is the drama.
acting.exits: Leaves by a screen edge into the next flip-screen room.
acting.depth: Tiny hero against a big dark room; giant creatures and pillars dwarf it.

techniques: dark default + small local light sources
one warm hero on a cool near-black palette
tiny hero vs giant creature for scale
procedural motion for an uncanny feel
feel: near-black cool room + one warm few-pixel hero + slow drifting motes = eerie wonder
for_fred: Put Fred small in a dark room with one light source near him and slow drifting specks; let a giant shape (a huge Pixie paw or eye) move in the background while Fred stays tiny. Use the dark scene as a quiet beat between busy ones.
